title: Michael Kayode says Juventus links are ‘nice’ but wants to ‘improve at Brentford’
content:
Brentford’s Michael Kayode says reported interest from Juventus is “nice” but he is “not thinking about going back to Italy.”

The 21-year-old right-back has been one of Brentford’s standout performers this season with showings leading to him being nominated for the Premier League Young Player of the Year award earlier this week.

The Italy under-21 international, who joined Brentford from Fiorentina in January 2025, has been linked with a move back to Serie A with Juventus reportedly interested in securing his services.

When asked about the reports, he told Tuttosport: “To be honest, I’m not thinking about going back to Italy: I just want to perform well, improve here at Brentford and continue to develop at this club.”

“Obviously, interest from Juventus – or any top club, for that matter – is always nice, but I’m fully focused on the final stages of the season.”

Kayode joined Brenford initially on loan before that deal was made permanent in the summer of 2025.

In his first full season in England, he has missed just one Premier League game and has put Brentford, eighth in the Premier League, on the cusp of achieving European qualification for the first time in the club’s history.

Kayode, who is well-known for the distance of his long throws, has represented Italy at under-18, under-19 and under-21 levels but is yet to make his senior debut for the nation team.

In an interview with The Athletic in March, Kayode said: “Brentford is a special team. The first time I went to the club, I felt like I was three or four years with the team. I love this club and for me, everything is so easy here.”

Brentford end their season with a home game against Crystal Palace on Sunday before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool on the final day on May 24.
